column2: Retain arrival at Soklag, David still kept away from Saul son of Kish and the men's military help. Kept away is the inherited contextual rendering of the constrained/separated participle, not an explicit imprisonment claim.
column3: Does the participle best describe confinement, restriction or refuge away from Saul in this construction?

column2: Retain right and left bow use, slingers with stones and bows and descent from Saul's Benjaminite brethren. Hands supplies the natural body-part referent; the mixed sling/bow construction remains unresolved rather than replacing bows with arrows.
column3: How does the repeated bow term connect to slingers, and is the current coordination clear enough to preserve the weapon distinction?

column2: Retain ruler Achiezer, Joas son of Asma, Joel and Jophalet sons of Asmoth, Berchia and Jeoul with affiliations. The selected singular son after Joas is not automatically extended to Achiezer.
Retain Samaias the Gabaonite, mighty among thirty and over thirty. Both selected thirty references remain rather than a three/thirty harmonization.
Retain Jermias, Jeziel, Joanan and Jozabad the Gadarathite in the continued list. The final affiliation stays attached to the immediately named man.
Retain Eliazai, Jarimouth, Baalia, Samaria and Saphatia the Charaiphite. No theological inference from Baalia's name changes its transliteration.
Retain five named Korites: Elkana, Jesouni, Ozriel, Joazar and Jesboam. The plural family label applies to the group rather than one newly inferred person.
Retain Elia and Zabadia, sons of Iraam and sons of Gedor. The selected sons-of-Gedor expression is not silently rewritten as from a town.

Retain the Gaddites' separation to David from the wilderness, battle strength, large shields, spears, lion faces and gazelle-like speed in mountains. The from direction is not changed to a wilderness destination, and the animal images remain.
Retain Azer as ruler, Abdia second and Eliab third. The numbered list remains a ranking without an inferred troop count for each man.
Retain Masemanne fourth and Jermia fifth. The later Jermia repetition is not grounds for removing this entry.
Retain Eththi sixth and Eliab seventh. Eliab remains repeated from third place rather than a duplicate corrected without evidence.
Retain Joanan eighth and Eliazer ninth. The ordinal progression is preserved.
Retain Jermia tenth and Machabannai eleventh. The repeated Jermia and total eleven named leaders remain.

Retain Gad's army rulers, a small one for the hundred and a great one for the thousand. The dative relationships are left open rather than asserting either command of those numbers or individual equivalence in fighting strength.
column3: Does the phrase rank commanders over hundreds/thousands or compare the fighting capacity of individual men?

column2: Retain first-month Jordan crossing, overflow of its entire bank and expulsion of all valley dwellers east to west. The flood circumstance and full directional range remain without a modern seasonal gloss.
Retain arrivals from Benjamin and Judah for David's aid. Some represents the source's partitive rather than implying a whole-tribe migration.

Retain the peace condition, heart freely inclined, betrayal condition, without truth of hand and the optative appeal that the fathers' God see and reprove. Freely inclined is an inherited interpretation of the heart-by-itself expression; the difficult hand clause is not replaced by a confident innocence statement.
column3: Whose hand is qualified by without truth, and how does that clause affect the betrayal condition?

column2: Retain an indefinite spirit clothing Amasai, ruler of thirty, the command to go, people, David son of Jesse, repeated peace and God's completed help. Propose display lines for the five speech units supported by the publisher's poetic layout, with narrative introduction and conclusion separate. No wording changes or divine identification of the spirit are imposed.
column3: Does the indefinite spirit denote divine empowerment or another motivating spirit? The source does not settle that by capitalization.

column2: Retain Manassite arrivals during the foreigners' movement against Saul, David not helping them and the generals' decision about those men's heads. Their quoted fear remains third-person those men rather than an imported our heads formula.
Retain the seven named Manassite leaders joining during the journey to Soklag and leadership of thousands. The two similar Jozabath/Josabeth forms remain separate entries.

Retain fighting alongside David against the Geddour, all as mighty and the repeated army/force leadership. Geddour remains an unresolved term rather than confidently identifying the raiding band from another narrative.
column3: Does geddour denote a raiding troop, a group name or something else in this selected clause?

column2: Retain day-after-day arrivals and a great force like God's force. Men and forming supply English clause connections; the comparison is not changed to an absolute statement that the army is divine.

Retain the names-of-army-rulers heading, Hebron and transfer of Saul's kingdom to David according to the Lord's word. Names remains the selected heading even though much of the following material enumerates tribal totals.
Retain Judah's large shields and spears, six thousand eight hundred and readiness in battle array. Both equipment types and the exact total remain.
Retain Simeon's strength for battle array and seven thousand one hundred. The figure is not combined with Judah's into a new total.
Retain Levi's four thousand six hundred. No separate military-role qualification is supplied in this shorter unit.
Retain Joadae as leader for Aaron and three thousand seven hundred with him. For Aaron remains the selected inherited relation rather than a confidently supplied descendant or priestly-family title.
Retain young Sadok's strength and twenty-two ancestral-house rulers. Young does not become an invented numerical age.

Retain Benjamin as Saul's brethren, three thousand and most still guarding Saul's house. The clause's group reference remains open; no contradiction is removed by reassigning most to a different unstated population.
Retain Ephraim's twenty thousand eight hundred, strength and renown by ancestral houses. The two descriptions of military standing remain distinct.
Retain half Manasseh's eighteen thousand and designation by name for David to reign. The purpose of the registration remains rather than an added claim that every named man personally anointed him.

Retain understanding of times, knowledge of what Israel should do, the leadership-related phrase, two hundred and all brethren with them. The selected leadership connection is not automatically converted to a simple two hundred chiefs heading.
column3: How does for their beginnings or leadership attach, and what is counted by two hundred?

column2: Retain Zaboulon's fifty thousand, every war weapon and aid to David without leaning another way. The final adverb expresses undivided support provisionally without importing an explicit double-heart phrase.
Retain Nephthali's one thousand rulers and thirty-seven thousand shield-and-spear bearers with them. The leaders and accompanying men remain distinct counts.
Retain Danite battle formation and twenty-eight thousand eight hundred. No rounding is introduced.
Retain Aser's forty thousand going out to help in war. The assistance purpose remains explicit.
Retain beyond-Jordan Reuben, Gaddi and half Manasseh, every war weapon and one hundred twenty thousand. The half-tribe designation and selected Gaddi form remain.

Retain warriors in battle order with a peaceful soul, Hebron, kingship over all Israel and the remainder as one soul. Peaceful is the selected description, not a replacement by perfect heart or an inferred absence of weapons.
Retain three days eating and drinking and preparation by their brethren. No ritual feast name or extra duration is supplied.

Retain neighboring donors as far as three named tribes, four carrying-animal types and the full food list with abundant calves and sheep. Calves occur both as carriers and as provisions; both selected occurrences remain, followed by the gladness explanation.
